facts.text: A virtual job site is a three-dimensional computer model of a mine, quarry or construction site in which simulated machines, sensors and people can be tested.
facts.quote: A virtual job site is a three-dimensional computer model of a mine, quarry or construction site in which simulated machines, sensors and people can be tested.

facts.text: A virtual job site must represent real workplace details faithfully, including berm height, ramp slope, rock-face color and roughness, and stockpile position.
facts.quote: it must be true to a real workplace: the height of a berm, the slope of a ramp, the color and roughness of a rock face, the position of a stockpile.

facts.text: Chapter 5 stresses that a useful virtual job site is a stack of connected models, not merely a 3D picture. Beyond appearance, the site needs correctly coordinated geometry, collision surfaces, sensor-specific material properties, stopping-distance-relevant ground mechanics, controllable moving actors, weather and airborne dust, and pixel or point labels.
facts.quote: it needs geometry in correct coordinates, collision surfaces so that the virtual machine cannot drive through a wall, material properties for each sensor type, ground mechanics that change stopping distance, moving actors with controllable behavior, weather and airborne dust, and labels

facts.text: A photorealistic virtual job site lacking the connected models required beyond appearance is not a valid sensor simulation.
facts.quote: A photorealistic scene that lacks these is not a valid sensor simulation [Chapter 5].

facts.text: Chapter 5 found eleven ways to build virtual job sites, including hand-built models, rule-based generation, drone photogrammetry, laser survey, reconstruction from machine recordings, neural and generative methods, reuse of mine plans, and ready-made asset libraries.
facts.quote: Chapter 5 found eleven ways to build sites, from hand-built models and rule-based generation to drone photogrammetry, laser survey, reconstruction from the machine's own recordings, neural and generative methods, reuse of mine plans and ready-made asset libraries.

facts.text: No single virtual-job-site construction method serves camera, radar, lidar and ultrasonic testing across 100 or more site types.
facts.quote: No single method serves camera, radar, lidar and ultrasonic testing across 100 or more site types;

facts.text: Chapter 5 concludes that the evidence points to a hybrid environment factory using parameterized representative site types anchored to a few surveyed real sites.
facts.quote: the evidence points to a hybrid "environment factory" of parameterized representative site types anchored to a few surveyed real sites [Chapter 5].

facts.text: No published method or standard sets the number of virtual job sites needed.
facts.quote: No published method or standard sets a number of sites;

facts.text: The booklet offers 15 to 30 virtual-job-site archetypes and 3 to 5 surveyed anchor sites as a planning assumption only, not an established required site count.
facts.quote: the booklet offers 15 to 30 archetypes and 3 to 5 surveyed anchor sites as a planning assumption only

facts.text: The booklet prefers a stopping criterion for virtual-job-site construction based on coverage of the operating domain rather than a fixed site count.
facts.quote: prefers a stop criterion based on coverage of the operating domain [Chapter 5].

facts.text: Virtual job sites can be built from October 2026 before sensors are chosen and reused later with whichever sensor models are selected.
facts.quote: Sites can be built from October 2026, before the sensors are chosen, and reused later with whichever sensor models are selected;

facts.text: The booklet recommends collecting reconstruction-quality machine logs immediately so virtual job sites can be built before sensor selection and reused with the selected sensor models.
facts.quote: the booklet recommends collecting reconstruction-quality machine logs now for that reason [Chapter 5].
